name: Driving Licence (Learner's)
eligibility: Age 16+ for motorcycles without gear (engine capacity up to 50cc) with parent/guardian consent; Age 18+ for light motor vehicles (LMV / cars / motorcycles with gear); Age 20+ for transport/commercial vehicles.
documents_required: Proof of Age (Birth Certificate, 10th School Marksheet, Passport, or PAN Card), Proof of Address (Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Utility Bill), Form 1 self-declaration of physical fitness, recent passport-size photographs.
steps: 1. Visit Parivahan Sarathi portal: https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/ and select your State. 2. Click 'Apply for Learner Licence'. 3. Fill applicant personal, address, and vehicle class details. 4. Upload scanned identity, address proof, photo, and signature. 5. Pay application and test fee online. 6. Book test appointment slot or take the online computerized LL test from home (where Aadhaar authentication is enabled). 7. Pass the test and download digital Learner's Licence immediately.
fees: ₹200 total (₹150 application fee + ₹50 learner test fee)
processing_time: Issued same day or within 24 to 48 hours upon passing test
notes: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Parivahan standards

name: Driving Licence (Permanent)
eligibility: Holders of a valid Learner's Licence who have completed a minimum of 30 days from LL issue date and apply within 180 days (6 months) validity period.
documents_required: Valid Learner's Licence, Form 4 application form, vehicle of the applied category for practical driving test, original age and address proof documents for verification.
steps: 1. Visit https://sarathi.parivahan.gov.in/ and select your State. 2. Click 'Apply for Driving Licence'. 3. Enter Learner's Licence number and Date of Birth. 4. Select vehicle class and fill required details. 5. Pay DL issuance fee online. 6. Book an appointment slot for the RTO driving skill test. 7. Appear at the RTO test track on the scheduled date with vehicle and driving instructor/original documents. 8. Upon passing practical driving test, DL is approved and smart card dispatched via Speed Post.
fees: ₹500 total (₹200 DL licence fee + ₹300 driving test fee; ₹200 extra for smart card form where applicable)
processing_time: Dispatched within 7 to 21 working days after passing driving test
notes: MoRTH Parivahan Sarathi standards

name: Aadhaar Enrolment
eligibility: Any Indian resident residing in India for 182 days or more in the preceding 12 months, including newborns, children, and adults.
documents_required: Proof of Identity (POI: Passport, PAN Card, Voter ID, Ration Card with photo, Driving Licence), Proof of Address (POA: Electricity Bill, Water Bill, Bank Passbook, Rent Agreement), Proof of Date of Birth (DOB: Birth Certificate, 10th School Marksheet, Passport).
steps: 1. Locate nearest authorized Aadhaar Enrolment Centre on UIDAI portal (appointments.uidai.gov.in). 2. Book appointment online or visit as walk-in. 3. Fill the Aadhaar Enrolment Form. 4. Submit original POI, POA, and DOB documents for verification. 5. Provide biometric data (10 fingerprints, iris scan, and live photograph). 6. Receive Enrolment Acknowledgement Slip with 28-digit Enrolment ID (EID). 7. Track status online on uidai.gov.in and download e-Aadhaar when generated.
fees: ₹0 (Completely Free of Cost for new enrolment)
processing_time: 15 to 30 working days
notes: Official UIDAI Enrolment procedure

name: Aadhaar PVC Card Order
eligibility: Any Aadhaar card holder wanting a durable, wallet-sized polyvinyl chloride (PVC) card with security features (QR code, hologram, microtext).
documents_required: Aadhaar number or 28-digit Enrolment ID (EID). Registered mobile number is optional (can use non-registered mobile for OTP authentication).
steps: 1. Visit myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in and select 'Order Aadhaar PVC Card'. 2. Enter 12-digit Aadhaar number and security captcha. 3. Verify via OTP sent to registered or alternate mobile number. 4. Preview Aadhaar details (available if registered mobile used). 5. Pay fee of ₹50 online via UPI, Net Banking, or Debit/Credit Card. 6. Download payment receipt containing Service Request Number (SRN). 7. Track delivery status on UIDAI portal.
fees: ₹50 (inclusive of GST and Speed Post delivery charges)
processing_time: Printed and dispatched within 5 working days; delivered by India Post within 7 to 15 days
notes: Official UIDAI PVC Card service

name: Property Registration
eligibility: Parties registering property or land (Buyer, Seller, Donor, Donee, or Power of Attorney holder) having legal title and capacity to contract; applicable state registration rules apply.
documents_required: Sale Deed or Conveyance Deed draft; Identity and Address Proof of Buyer, Seller, and Two Witnesses (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID); Latest Land Record or Record of Rights (Jamabandi / 7-12 / Khatauni); Encumbrance Certificate (EC); Property Tax Receipts; and Proof of Stamp Duty and Registration Fee payment.
steps: 1. Access the National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS) portal (https://ngdrs.gov.in/) or your State Registration & Stamps portal (e.g. IGRS). 2. Register or login and calculate applicable Stamp Duty and Registration Fee based on circle rate or guidance value. 3. Pay Stamp Duty and Registration Fee online via e-Stamping / GRAS and upload draft deed and KYC proofs. 4. Book an appointment slot at the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) having jurisdiction over the property. 5. Both parties and two witnesses appear at the Sub-Registrar Office with original documents for biometric verification and photograph. 6. Sub-Registrar registers the deed; registered property document is issued and accessible online.
fees: Stamp Duty (typically 3% to 7% of property valuation depending on state and gender) plus 1% Registration Fee
processing_time: Same day or 1 to 3 working days after Sub-Registrar Office appointment and biometric execution
notes: Sub-Registrar Office Property and Land Registration

name: Liquor Licence (Commercial / Bar / Restaurant / Retail Shop)
eligibility: Indian citizens aged 21 or 25+ (depending on State Excise Act), sole proprietors, partnership firms, or registered companies with no criminal or excise convictions and proven financial solvency.
documents_required: Identity proof (Aadhaar & PAN), premises ownership title deed or registered commercial rent lease, building floor plan approved by local authority, Fire Safety NOC, Municipal Trade Licence, GST Registration, FSSAI Food Licence, Police Character Verification certificate, and bank solvency certificate.
steps: 1. Visit the respective State Excise / e-Abkari Online Portal (e.g., excise.punjab.gov.in, stateexcise.maharashtra.gov.in, delhiexcise.gov.in, kldc.kerala.gov.in). 2. Register as a business entity and select the required liquor licence category (L-1/L-2 retail vend, L-4/L-5 restaurant/hotel bar). 3. Fill the comprehensive application form with premises, applicant, and partnership/corporate details. 4. Upload mandatory identity proofs, premises blueprint layout, Fire NOC, and solvency certificate. 5. Pay initial scrutiny and inspection fee online. 6. Joint site inspection conducted by Excise Inspector and Municipal authorities to verify distance from schools, places of worship, and highways. 7. Upon approval by District Collector / Excise Commissioner, pay prescribed annual license fee and receive Liquor Licence.
fees: Varies by state, area tier, and category: Typically ₹50,000 to ₹10,00,000+ per annum depending on location and category
processing_time: 30 to 60 working days
notes: State Excise Department commercial licensing

name: Occasional / Temporary / Event Liquor Permit
eligibility: Individuals aged 21/25+ or registered event organizers hosting a private party, wedding celebration, banquet, or social function where alcohol will be served.
documents_required: Applicant Aadhaar Card and PAN Card, venue booking receipt / NOC from hotel, club, banquet hall, or farmhouse, function date, time, and estimated guest attendance.
steps: 1. Access the State Excise Department online portal (e.g., Form FL-4 in Maharashtra, Form P-10 in Delhi, Form L-50 in Punjab/Haryana). 2. Select 'Apply for Temporary / Occasional / Party Liquor Permit'. 3. Fill function details: date, duration, venue address, and number of guests. 4. Upload applicant ID proof and banquet/venue booking confirmation letter. 5. Pay the online daily permit fee. 6. Instant or 24-hour approval; download the digital Occasional Liquor Permit. 7. Procure liquor only from authorized licensed vends and display the permit copy at the venue bar counter during the event.
fees: Varies by state and guest count: Typically ₹2,000 to ₹15,000 per day/event
processing_time: 1 to 3 working days (often issued same day online)
notes: State Excise Department temporary party permit

name: Personal Liquor Permit / Consumption Permit
eligibility: Adult citizens or domestic/international tourists (aged 25+ in Maharashtra) purchasing, transporting, or consuming liquor for personal use where mandated by state excise laws.
documents_required: Applicant Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / Passport, proof of age, passport-size photograph, and medical fitness declaration (where required by state rule).
steps: 1. Visit the State Excise online portal (e.g. stateexcise.maharashtra.gov.in for Form FL-X / FL-IV). 2. Register with mobile number and select 'Personal Liquor Permit'. 3. Upload photo, ID proof, and address proof. 4. Pay prescribed permit fee online. 5. Download the digital Liquor Permit certificate immediately with QR code.
fees: ₹100 for 1-year permit; ₹1,000 for lifetime permit (Maharashtra); nominal for 1-day tourist permits
processing_time: Same day / Instant digital download
notes: State Excise Department personal consumption permit

name: Arms / Gun Licence Application (NDAL-ALIS)
eligibility: Indian citizens aged 21 years or older, of sound mind, with no record of criminal conviction or history of domestic violence, demonstrating genuine self-defence need, threat perception, or registered sports shooting credentials.
documents_required: Form A-1 application form, Proof of Identity (Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID), Proof of Residence, Medical Fitness Certificate (Form S-3) signed by registered medical practitioner, Police Character Verification report, two guarantor references, Safe Storage Locker declaration, and proof of income/IT returns.
steps: 1. Visit the Ministry of Home Affairs NDAL-ALIS portal (https://ndal-alis.gov.in/) or District Magistrate e-Services portal. 2. Register and select 'Apply for New Arms Licence' (Form A-1). 3. Fill personal credentials, reason for firearm requirement, and weapon category (e.g. Non-Prohibited Bore). 4. Upload medical fitness certificate, identity/address proofs, and photograph. 5. Pay application fee. 6. Attend local police station verification and CID/Special Branch inquiry. 7. Appear for personal interview before District Magistrate / Licensing Authority. 8. Upon grant, purchase firearm from authorized dealer within prescribed period and register weapon number on portal.
fees: ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 application and renewal fees depending on weapon type (Pistol, Revolver, Rifle)
processing_time: 60 to 90 working days
notes: Ministry of Home Affairs NDAL-ALIS arms licensing

name: Trade Licence (Municipal Shop & Commercial Establishment)
eligibility: Any business proprietor, merchant, or company operating a commercial trade, shop, or service establishment within municipal corporation or municipal council limits.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, premises ownership deed or registered rent lease with landlord NOC, property tax paid receipt, establishment layout sketch, and Fire Safety NOC where applicable.
steps: 1. Visit your city municipal corporation portal (e.g. MCD Delhi, BMC Mumbai, BBMP Bengaluru, or state urban development portal). 2. Select 'Apply for Trade Licence / Shop License'. 3. Fill shop and business category details. 4. Upload premises ownership/rent docs and ID proof. 5. Pay municipal licence fees based on business category and area. 6. Municipal inspector conducts site verification if needed. 7. Download digitally signed Trade Licence.
fees: ₹1,000 to ₹10,000 depending on city tier, trade category, and square footage
processing_time: 7 to 15 working days
notes: Urban Local Body municipal trade licensing

name: Fire Safety Certificate / Fire NOC
eligibility: Owners, builders, or occupants of commercial establishments, restaurants, assembly halls, schools, hospitals, hotels, and high-rise residential/commercial buildings.
documents_required: Sanctioned building architectural drawings, fire fighting equipment layout, fire extinguisher test certificates, building completion certificate, and site photographs.
steps: 1. Access State Fire and Emergency Services portal. 2. Apply for Fire Safety Provisional / Final NOC. 3. Upload sanctioned building plans and fire equipment installations. 4. Pay inspection fee. 5. Fire Officer conducts physical site inspection to verify hydrants, sprinklers, and emergency exits. 6. Fire Safety NOC issued online.
fees: ₹2,000 to ₹25,000+ based on building height and floor area
processing_time: 15 to 30 working days
notes: State Fire and Emergency Services compliance

name: Senior Citizen Certificate / Identity Card
eligibility: Indian citizens aged 60 years or older.
documents_required: Proof of Age (Birth Certificate, Voter ID, Passport, or 10th marksheet), Proof of Residence (Aadhaar Card, Ration Card, Electricity Bill), 2 passport-size photographs, and Blood Group report.
steps: 1. Visit State e-District portal or local District Social Welfare Office / Tehsildar office. 2. Submit Senior Citizen Card application form. 3. Attach age proof and address proof. 4. Verification completed by revenue/welfare officer. 5. Collect Senior Citizen ID Card for concessions in state transport, healthcare, and welfare programs.
fees: ₹0 (Completely Free of Cost)
processing_time: 7 to 15 working days
notes: Social Welfare Department senior citizen benefits

name: Unique Disability ID (UDID) Card & Certificate
eligibility: Persons with benchmark disabilities (40% or more) as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act 2016.
documents_required: Proof of Identity (Aadhaar Card), Address Proof, Disability Medical Certificate from authorized government hospital (if already available), recent passport photograph, and signature/thumb impression.
steps: 1. Visit the National UDID portal: https://www.swavlambancard.gov.in/. 2. Click 'Apply for Disability Certificate & UDID Card'. 3. Fill personal, address, and disability details. 4. Upload photo, signature, and identity documents. 5. Schedule appointment at designated District Medical Hospital for assessment. 6. Medical board evaluates disability percentage. 7. UDID card generated and dispatched by speed post, with digital card downloadable immediately.
fees: ₹0 (Completely Free of Cost)
processing_time: 15 to 30 working days
notes: DEPwD Ministry of Social Justice UDID project

name: Economically Weaker Section (EWS) Certificate
eligibility: General category citizens not covered under SC/ST/OBC reservations, whose family gross annual income is below ₹8 Lakh and who meet agricultural land/residential plot limits prescribed by government.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, family income certificates / salary slips / ITR, land and property documents (Khasra/Khatauni), ration card, and self-declaration affidavit.
steps: 1. Apply online on State e-District portal or at local Tehsildar / Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office. 2. Fill EWS income and asset application form. 3. Upload or submit income and land records. 4. Field verification conducted by Patwari / Revenue Inspector. 5. Download verified EWS Income and Asset Certificate from portal.
fees: ₹10 to ₹50 nominal state portal charges
processing_time: 15 to 21 working days
notes: Revenue Department EWS quota certification

name: Legal Heir Certificate / Surviving Member Certificate
eligibility: Spouse, children, or surviving parents of a deceased family member.
documents_required: Death Certificate of the deceased person, Identity and Address proofs of all surviving legal heirs, Family tree / genealogy affidavit on stamp paper, and ration card.
steps: 1. Visit State e-District or local Tehsildar office. 2. Fill Legal Heir Application form. 3. Attach death certificate and all heirs' identity proofs. 4. Notice published and revenue inquiry conducted by Village Administrative Officer / Revenue Inspector. 5. Legal Heir Certificate issued signed by Tehsildar / SDM.
fees: ₹20 to ₹100 nominal fee
processing_time: 15 to 30 working days
notes: Revenue Department legal heir certification

name: Caste Validity Certificate
eligibility: Students and job applicants belonging to SC, ST, OBC, or VJNT categories who hold a Caste Certificate and require validation for higher education admissions or reserved government employment.
documents_required: Original Caste Certificate, applicant's primary school leaving certificate, father's and grandfather's school leaving / revenue records mentioning caste, genealogical family tree (Vamshavali) affidavit, and Aadhaar card.
steps: 1. Visit the State Caste Scrutiny Committee portal (e.g. BARTI CCVIS in Maharashtra, or state social welfare portal). 2. Register application for Caste Certificate Scrutiny. 3. Upload genealogical family tree affidavit and historical caste proof documents. 4. Submit application through college/employer or directly. 5. Scrutiny committee examines ancestral records and may conduct police vigilance cell inquiry. 6. Scrutiny committee approves and issues Caste Validity Certificate.
fees: Nominal application fee (₹50 to ₹100)
processing_time: 30 to 90 working days
notes: Social Justice Department caste validity scrutiny
